questions.question: Which of the motions is passed in the parliament to remove the President of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Impeachment Motion**__.

 
• An impeachment motion is passed in the parliament to remove the** President of India.**
 
• The impeachment is a **quasi-judicial procedure.**
 
• **Article 61** of the Indian constitution deals with the processes of impeachment of the president.
 
• The only ground for the impeachment of the president is "**violation of the constitution**".
 
• The impeachment procedure can be initiated by either house of the parliament.
 
• The charges are contained in a notice that should be signed by **one-fourth** of the total members of the initiating house.
 
• A **14 days advance notice** should be given to the president after initiating the procedure.
 
• The president can defend himself by taking the service of the attorney general of India or any other law officer of his choice.
 
• The impeachment procedure requires a special majority.
 
• If the other house also passes a resolution by **2/3 majority** of the total members of the house, then the president will be removed from his office from the date on which the bill is so passed.
 
• **No president **has so far impeached in India.

questions.question: A bill becomes an Act of the Parliament after being passed by both the houses of Parliament and assented to by the ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **A bill becomes an Act of the Parliament after being passed by both the Houses of Parliament and assented to by the President.**
 
• The basic function of Parliament is to make laws. All legislative proposals have to be brought in the form of Bills before Parliament.
 
• A Bill is a statute in the draft and cannot become law unless it has received the approval of both the Houses of Parliament and the assent of the President of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The process of law-making **begins with the** introduction of a Bill in either House of Parliament. **
 
• **A Bill can be introduced either by a Minister or a member other than a Minister. **
 
• **In the former case, it is called a Government Bill and in the latter case, it is known as a Private Member's Bill.**
 
• A Bill undergoes three readings in each House, i.e., the Lok Sabha and the Rajya Sabha before it is submitted to the President for assent.
 
• **First Reading**
 
 
• The First Reading refers to
 
• (i) motion for leave to introduce a Bill in the House on the adoption of which the Bill is introduced.
 
• (ii) in the case of a Bill originated in and passed by the other House, the laying on the Table of the House of the Bill, as passed by the other House.
 
 
 
• **Second Reading**
 
• **Third Reading**
 
 
• The Third Reading refers to the discussion on the motion that the Bill or the Bill, as amended, be passed.
 
 
 
• **An almost similar procedure is followed in Rajya Sabha in respect of Bills introduced in that House.**
 
• **After a Bill has been finally passed by the Houses of Parliament, it is submitted to the President for his assent. **
 
• **After a Bill has received the assent of the President, it becomes the law of the land.**

questions.question: Who has the power to grant pardon, respite, postponement or remission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**Pardoning powers -**

__
 
• The** President of India has the power to grant pardons, reprieves, respites, or remissions of punishme**nt.
 
• This p**ower is granted to the President by Article 7**2 of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The** President can grant pardons to convicted peop**le, including those sentenced to death.
 
• The Presiden**t can also reduce the sentence of a convicted person.**
 
• The President **can exercise this power based on the advice of the Council of Ministers.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​President's power to grant pardon procedure:

 
 
• In order to get the Cabinet's approval, Rashtrapati Bhawan sends the Home Ministry the compassion request.
 
• In turn, the Ministry sends this to the state government in question; based on the response, it formulates its recommendation on behalf of the Council of Ministers.
 
 
 
• Limitation:
 
 
• The President cannot use his pardoning authority without the consent of the executive branch.
 
• The President must follow the Council of Ministers' recommendations when choosing whether to grant a mercy plea, the Supreme Court has found in a number of cases.
 
 
 
• Pardon:
 
 
• A pardon totally exonerates the offender of all sentences, punishments, and disqualifications by eliminating both the penalty and the conviction.
 
 
 
• Commutation:
 
 
• It means that a harsher kind of punishment has been replaced with a less severe one.
 
 
 
• Remission:
 
 
• It suggests shortening the sentence without altering its content.
 
• For instance, a sentence of two years of hard labor could be reduced to one year of hard labor.
 
 
 
• Reprieve:
 
 
• It refers to substituting a reduced sentence for one that was initially imposed owing to a unique circumstance, such as a convict's physical impairment or a woman offender's pregnancy.

Under Article 72 of the constitution of India President has the power to Pardon, Commute, Remit, Respite and Reprieve the sentence. 

 
• Pardon - President can pardon the sentence of any convicted person and bring him to the position where all his deeds of crime will not carry any punishment. 
 
• Commute - President can reward lesser punishment to the person in place of rigorous punishment.
 
• Remit - by remitting the power President lessen the term of imprisonment. 
 
• Respite - In this, the President considers some cases and decrease the punishment of the offender. 
 
• Reprieve - In case of a death sentence, the President can hold the punishment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: The Chief Justice of India will take prior permission from the _____________, while appointing Adhoc Judges.
questions.solution:

__
 
• According to the **Constitution of India**, the **Chief Justice of India** (CJI) is required to seek the prior permission of the **President of India** before appointing **Adhoc Judges** in the Supreme Court of India.
 
• An Ad hoc judge is a Supreme Court judge appointed by a procedure for a specific project or case for a specific period of time.
 
• **When a quorum of permanent judges is required to continue or hold a Supreme Court session, Article 127 of the Indian Constitution proposes that the Chief Justice of India can appoint a High Court judge as an ad hoc Supreme Court judge for a specified time.**
 
• **The Supreme Court Chief Justice can only do so after consulting with the Chief Justice of the High Court in question and receiving the President's prior consent.**
 
• The judge chosen for this position must be eligible to sit on the Indian Supreme Court.
 
• Above all other obligations, it is the judge so designated's responsibility to attend Supreme Court sessions.
 
• **In doing so, the Ad hoc judge in India has all of the power, authority, benefits, and obligations of a Supreme Court judge.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ad hoc Judges' Role:**

 
 
• Cases that are more than five years old are usually assigned to ad hoc judges. Regardless, it would not be inappropriate for the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court to exercise his discretion in hearing such cases.
 
• It is not necessary to form a divisional bench of Ad hoc Judges and Sitting Judges in cases to be heard before the Division Bench. At the moment, the Division Bench may only be made up of ad hoc judges because these are old cases that need to be heard.
 
 
 
• 
 Because an ad hoc judge's role is to carry out the functions of a Supreme Court Justice, it would be inappropriate for an ad hoc judge to perform any other permitted work.

questions.question: When the President of India keeps a bill (except money bill and constitutional amendment bill) pending for an indefinite period, it is called ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**pocket veto of the President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A pocket veto** is the term used when the **Indian president **delays a law indefinitely. 
 
• A pocket veto is a type of legislative technique that permits the president to veto a bill without actually acting on it. This basically vetoes the law without giving it a positive vote. 
 
• The bill is neither rejected by the president nor sent back for more examination. The President is not subject to a time constraint under the Constitution to act on the bill. 
 
• Gyani Zail Singh was the first president to exercise a pocket veto.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• When a president receives a measure and is unable to reject it and send it back to Congress within ten days, this is known as a pocket veto.
 
• Despite the absence of official objections and a signature, the bill does not become law.
 
• The veto override procedure in Congress does not apply to pocket vetoes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• A simple majority can override a suspensive veto, sometimes referred to as a suspensory veto.
 
• The ability to refuse to provide the president of India's consent to a measure that has been passed by parliament is known as the absolute veto.
 
• The president can offer suggestions for improving a measure through an amendatory veto. Within ten days of the bill's passing, the president is required to veto it.

questions.question: In the states, No Demand for Grants can be made EXCEPT on the recommendation of the ____________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Governor **__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Governor's Role:**

 
 
• In the states, **No Demand for Grants** can be made except on the recommendation of the **Governor**.
 
• This provision is outlined in **Article 203(3)** of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The Governor, as the constitutional head of the state, ensures that financial proposals align with the state's fiscal policies.
 
• The recommendation is a safeguard to maintain financial discipline and accountability.
 
• The Governor's approval is mandatory before any demand for grants is presented in the state legislature.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chief Minister:**

 
 
• The **Chief Minister** is the head of the state government and plays a key role in formulating policies and budgets.
 
• However, the Chief Minister does not have the constitutional authority to recommend demands for grants.
 
• The Chief Minister works closely with the Finance Minister to prepare the budget and financial proposals.
 
• While the Chief Minister influences financial decisions, the final recommendation must come from the Governor.
 
• The Chief Minister's role is executive, whereas the Governor's role is constitutional in this context.
 
 
 
• **Finance Minister of the State:**
 
 
• The **Finance Minister** is responsible for preparing the state budget and overseeing financial matters.
 
• The Finance Minister presents the budget and demands for grants in the state legislature.
 
• However, the Finance Minister cannot recommend demands for grants without the Governor's approval.
 
• The Finance Minister works under the guidance of the Chief Minister and the state cabinet.
 
• The recommendation for demands for grants is a constitutional function reserved for the Governor.
 
 
 
• **President of India:**
 
 
• The **President of India** is the constitutional head of the country and does not directly intervene in state financial matters.
 
• The President's role in financial matters is limited to the central government and union territories.
 
• State financial procedures, including demands for grants, are governed by the state Governor, not the President.
 
• The President's approval is required for central government expenditures, not state-level demands for grants.
 
• The President's role is distinct from that of the Governor in state financial processes.

• This election is conducted through the system of proportional representation by means of the single transferable vote method.
 
• To ensure fairness and equity, each vote is given suitable weightage to maintain uniformity among states and parity between the states and the Union.
 
• The President must fulfill certain eligibility criteria, including being a citizen of India, at least 35 years of age, and qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha.
 
• Their term of office spans five years, and they are eligible for re-election. Removal from office follows the procedure outlined in Article 61 of the Constitution.
